output.review_comment:
Two fixes look right: the divisibility check (ValueError when slot_minutes doesn't divide 1440 evenly) and wrapping 24:00 to "00:00". Both were already required by the docstring.

The blocker is that the PR also changes the rounding rule. The documented rule, which the old integer formula `(2*m + s) // (2*s)` implemented, is that a time exactly halfway between two slots rounds up to the later one. The PR replaces this with Python's `round()`, which rounds halfway cases to the even slot index, and rewrites the docstring to match. With 30-minute slots, 01:15 now snaps to 01:00 instead of 01:30. The docstring is the written form of the spec agreed with the workplace team, so editing it to fit new code is the wrong way round. If a test really expects round-half-to-even, it conflicts with the documented contract, and a human should resolve that with the workplace team. If no test needs it, this is an unrequested change to what users see. There is also no PR description saying which tests failed or why.

Suggested fix: keep integer round-half-up, add the divisibility check and the wrap (`snapped = (index * slot_minutes) % MINUTES_PER_DAY`), and leave the docstring unchanged. This also avoids floating-point division. If any test still fails, report the conflict between the test and the docstring instead of changing the rounding rule.
